title: Netherlands – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Architectenselectie ver-/nieuwbouw Montessori Vaklyceum
description: De opdracht betreft de architectonische uitwerking van de vernieuwbouw, inclusief de buitenruimte, van het Montessori Vaklyceum aan de Vondellaan 83 in Groningen. De opgave omvat de voorbereiding, het ontwerp en de verdere uitwerking van een toekomstbestendige onderwijshuisvesting, passend bij de ambities van Openbaar Onderwijs Groningen en de gemeente Groningen. De vernieuwbouw bestaat uit het behoud van circa 1.300 m² van het bestaande gebouw uit 1968 en de realisatie van circa 4.000 m² nieuwbouw, gezamenlijk circa 5.300 m² BVO. Het bestaande bouwdeel uit 1968 vertegenwoordigt een belangrijke cultuurhistorische waarde en vormt daarmee niet slechts een bestaand gebouw dat behouden blijft, maar een wezenlijk vertrekpunt voor de ontwerpopgave. Naast het gebouw maakt ook de directe buitenruimte onderdeel uit van de ontwerpopgave.

buyer: Road Traffic Office of the Canton of Zurich
title: Production equipment for manufacturing vehicle license plates
description:
The Road Traffic Office of the Canton of Zurich has commissioned the Pöschwies Correctional Facility in Regensdorf to manufacture cantonal vehicle license plates. To fulfill this production mandate effectively over the long term—ensuring economic viability and impeccable quality—it is necessary to procure modern production equipment, relevant system accessories, and associated services.




The subject of this tender is the selection of a capable supplier for:


Embossing presses: High-performance machines for license plate production, including necessary operational accessories.

Embossing dies and storage: Complete sets of embossing dies and suitable, organized storage systems for safe and efficient handling.

Hot-stamping machines: Specialized machines for the precise coloring of embossed license plates.

Staff training: Comprehensive training and instruction for the facility's operating personnel to ensure safe and professional operation of all equipment.

Maintenance and support (SLA): Conclusion of a Service Level Agreement to ensure ongoing maintenance, periodic inspections, and rapid troubleshooting for maximum operational reliability.



The machinery, tools, and services to be supplied must be fully suitable for the production of Swiss vehicle license plates. They must strictly comply with all applicable technical specifications and defined quality standards for Swiss license plates.




The objective of this tender is to conclude a supply contract covering delivery, installation, commissioning, and training, as well as a separate Service Level Agreement (SLA) for ongoing maintenance.

buyer: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark
title: Consultancy framework agreement for formulation, appraisal and review of Danish development cooperation programmes and projects
description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (MFA) is in the process of streamlining the management of its development cooperation. Part of this effort concerns the simplification of the procurement process of key consultancy services relating to development cooperation. Consultancy contracts are currently procured individually by the case worker responsible for the programme or project. Case workers are MFA staff from MFA Services at Home and Services Abroad. They are responsible for the procurement process of individual contracts which is often lengthy, and can have implications on programme and project implementation timelines. Moreover, the fragmentation of the process makes it difficult to use the feedback from case workers on the fulfilment of the assignments. This makes it challenging to harvest learning from past performance and ensure a sustained quality of services. It is in this context that the MFA wishes to consolidate the procurement of consultancy services through a framework agreement with multiple contractors. The streamlining of the management of Danish development cooperation entailed a revision of the Danida – Aid Management Guidelines (AMG). This foresees a delegation of key tasks to external consultants, primarily appraisals, and thereby an expected rise in the number of consultancy services to be requested. It is therefore an opportune time to seek a more streamlined procurement process of consultancy services. The AMG’s Bilateral Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/guidelines-for-programmes-projects-country-strategic-frameworks-and-hard-earmarked-multilat-support) and Financial Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/financial-management) constitute the basic set of procedures for all Danish bilateral development cooperation. The guidelines outline the processes and requirements for the preparation, formulation, quality assurance, approval, implementation, completion and closure of Danish bilateral programmes and projects. The purpose of the framework agreement is to make the MFA procurement of key consultancy services relating to Danish bilateral development programmes and projects more effective and efficient by ensuring quick access to relevant specialists, reducing the procurement time for assignments, and improving the quality of services provided. The objective of the framework agreement is to have a contractual set-up between the MFA and a number of contractors who can provide, upon demand and in a timely manner, the required expertise and service quality for the formulation, appraisal and review of Danish bilateral development programmes and projects. The objective of each assignment and the required outputs will be described in the Terms of Reference, which will be part of the Delivery Contract for the individual assignment. The Framework Agreement solely covers Denmark’s bilateral development cooperation programmes and projects. Therefore, the scope of work of consultancy services solely pertains to Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds. The framework agreement is divided into two lots that reflect the thematic areas and priorities of Denmark’s Strategy for Development Cooperation: Lot 1: Climate, environment, private sector and financing. Lot 2: Governance, fragility, and migration. The framework agreement will require the provision of the following services pertaining to the design and implementation phases of bilateral development cooperation programmes, namely: Formulation of bilateral programmes and projects. This may include preparatory work in the formulation process if and as needed. Appraisal of the design of bilateral programmes and projects as a quality assurance milestone prior to approval. This includes external appraisals led by the consultant and early appraisals of larger or high-risk programmes/projects led by LÆRING. Review of bilateral programmes and projects under implementation. This can span inception, midterm and technical reviews covering the full implementation period of the programme/project as part of the MFA unit’s monitoring and reporting cycle. Reviews do not have the same scope of work, methodology and methods as an evaluation. The MFA’s definition of appraisal, review and evaluation services is aligned with the definitions provided by OECD/DAC (https://one.oecd.org/document/DCD/DAC/EV(2022)2/en/pdf). The content of the services will vary and be defined by the MFA in the specific Terms of Reference for each individual assignment. The following themes and types of services will not be part of the framework agreement: Research and university partnerships. Training programmes and tracer studies. Culture. NGO strategic partnership agreements with the MFA (SPA agreements). Core support to multilateral organisations as described in Danish Organisation Strategies. Strategic Sector Cooperation. Audit assignments. Legal assessments. Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) unit contracts and multi-year MEAL technical assistance. Evaluations. Tender process consultancies. Please refer to the Consultancy Framework Agreement and Appendix 1 Scope of Services for a more detailed description of the object of the procurement.

title: Greece – Cleaning and sanitation services in urban or rural areas, and related services – Υπηρεσίες αποκομιδής απορριμμάτων και καθαριότητας κοινόχρηστων χώρων Δήμου Άνδρου
description: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης είναι : • Καθαρισμός και ευπρεπισμός κοινοχρήστων χώρων των οικισμών του Δήμου, όπου προβλέπονται να γίνουν όλες οι απαιτούμενες εργασίες περισυλλογής ελεύθερων απορριμμάτων – ασπρίσματα – εργασίες πρασίνου - καθαρισμοί –και γενικός ευπρεπισμός των κοινόχρηστων χώρων, των δρόμων, πεζοδρόμων και πλατειών των οικισμών του Δήμου. • Αποψιλώσεις – κλαδέματα – καθαρισμοί από αυτοφυή βλάστηση, δημοτικών οδών, μονοπατιών και κοινόχρηστων χώρων στις εκτός σχεδίου περιοχές του Δήμου. (Η επιλογή των προς καθαρισμό περιοχών θα γίνεται από τον αρμόδιο αντιδήμαρχο, με βασικά κριτήρια την πυροπροστασία περιμετρικά των οικισμών και την ασφαλή διέλευση οχημάτων και πεζών) • Περισυλλογή των ειδικών κάδων κομποστοποίησης και αντικατάσταση τους με κενούς, σε επιλεγμένα σημεία των οικισμών Όρμου Κορθίου και Κορθίου, σύμφωνα με το πρόγραμμα κομποστοποίησης οργανικών αποβλήτων (υπολείμματα κουζίνας) του Δήμου Άνδρου. Για την εκτέλεση των ανωτέρω υπηρεσιών, ο ανάδοχος θα πρέπει να διαθέτει: Α) κατάλληλο προσωπικό: • 14 εργάτες καθαριότητας Β) απαιτούμενο υλικοτεχνικό εξοπλισμό: • Σακούλες απορριμμάτων μαύρες μεγάλες 120Χ120 εκ. & σακούλες μικρές για τα καλαθάκια • Ασβέστες για το άσπρισμα των οδών • Λοιπά υλικά και εργαλεία (βούρτσες, σκούπες, καρότσια ,κλπ) για τον καθαρισμό των οδών • Υλικοτεχνικό εξοπλισμό για τις εργασίες αποψίλωσης και κλαδεμάτων (χορτοκοπτικά, φτυάρια, πριόνια χειρός και βενζίνης, τσάπες, σκάλες κλπ) • Μέσα ατομικά προστασίας για τους εργαζόμενους. Για τις λοιπές ανάγκες του έργου, όπως περιγράφονται στην παρούσα, ο Δήμος θα παραχωρεί στον ανάδοχο κατάλληλα οχήματά του, αναλόγως των αναγκών και της διαθεσιμότητας. Ο ανάδοχος για την εκτέλεση των ανωτέρω εργασιών υποχρεούται να απασχολεί εργάτες καθαριότητας με εξαρτημένη σχέση εργασίας και με πλήρες ωράριο εργασίας, ως ακολούθως: - από την υπογραφή της σύμβασης και για χρονική διάρκεια 18 μηνών : 468 ημέρες x 14 εργάτες καθαριότητας = 6.552 ημερομίσθια με πλήρες ωράριο εργασίας, για τις εργασίες αποκομιδής απορριμμάτων και καθαριότητας κοινοχρήστων χώρων Δήμου Άνδρου(6 ήμερη απασχόληση). ΣΥΝΟΛΟ ημερομισθίων: 6.552. Η αρχική διάρκεια της σύμβασης ορίζεται σε δεκαοκτώ (18) μήνες από την ημερομηνία έναρξης ισχύος της, με ανώτατο αρχικό φυσικό αντικείμενο 6.552 ημερομισθίων πλήρους απασχόλησης και ανώτατη αρχική συμβατική αξία 511.711,20 € χωρίς ΦΠΑ. Η Αναθέτουσα Αρχή διατηρεί δικαίωμα προαίρεσης, το οποίο μπορεί να ασκηθεί, εν όλω ή εν μέρει, με αιτιολογημένη απόφαση του αρμοδίου οργάνου πριν από τη λήξη της αρχικής συμβατικής διάρκειας, εφόσον εξακολουθούν να υφίστανται ανάγκες παροχής των ίδιων υπηρεσιών και εξασφαλίζεται η απαιτούμενη δημοσιονομική κάλυψη. Το δικαίωμα προαίρεσης αφορά πρόσθετη διάρκεια έως εννέα (9) μήνες, πρόσθετο φυσικό αντικείμενο έως 3.276 ημερομίσθια πλήρους απασχόλησης και πρόσθετη αξία έως 255.855,60 € χωρίς ΦΠΑ, ήτοι έως ποσοστό 50% του αρχικού φυσικού και οικονομικού αντικειμένου. Σε περίπτωση πλήρους άσκησης της προαίρεσης, η συνολική διάρκεια της σύμβασης δεν μπορεί να υπερβεί τους είκοσι επτά (27) μήνες, ο συνολικός αριθμός ημερομισθίων τα 9.828 και η συνολική αξία τα 767.566,80 € χωρίς ΦΠΑ. Η άσκηση της προαίρεσης δεν μπορεί να μεταβάλει τη συνολική φύση της σύμβασης και αφορά αποκλειστικά τις υπηρεσίες και τις τεχνικές προδιαγραφές που περιγράφονται εξαρχής στα συμβατικά τεύχη. Ο Δήμος δύναται να αναπροσαρμόζει την κατανομή των ημερομισθίων τόσο ανά Δημοτική Ενότητα (χωρικά), όσο και ανά χρονική περίοδο (χρονικά), αναλόγως των αναγκών του Δήμου. Η παρεχόμενη υπηρεσία κατατάσσεται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων (CPV): 90600000-3 : “Υπηρεσίες καθαριότητας και εξυγίανσης σε αστικές ή αγροτικές ζώνες, καθώς και συναφείς υπηρεσίες” Αναλυτική περιγραφή του φυσικού και οικονομικού αντικειμένου της σύμβασης δίδεται στο ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ Α της παρούσας διακήρυξης. (αρ. μελέτης: 10/2026) Η σύμβαση θα ανατεθεί με το κριτήριο της πλέον συμφέρουσας από οικονομική άποψη προσφοράς, βάσει της τιμής.

buyer: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark
title: Denmark – Foreign economic-aid-related services – Consultancy framework agreement for formulation, appraisal and review of Danish development cooperation programmes and projects
description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (MFA) is in the process of streamlining the management of its development cooperation. Part of this effort concerns the simplification of the procurement process of key consultancy services relating to development cooperation. Consultancy contracts are currently procured individually by the case worker responsible for the programme or project. Case workers are MFA staff from MFA Services at Home and Services Abroad. They are responsible for the procurement process of individual contracts which is often lengthy, and can have implications on programme and project implementation timelines. Moreover, the fragmentation of the process makes it difficult to use the feedback from case workers on the fulfilment of the assignments. This makes it challenging to harvest learning from past performance and ensure a sustained quality of services. It is in this context that the MFA wishes to consolidate the procurement of consultancy services through a framework agreement with multiple contractors. The streamlining of the management of Danish development cooperation entailed a revision of the Danida – Aid Management Guidelines (AMG). This foresees a delegation of key tasks to external consultants, primarily appraisals, and thereby an expected rise in the number of consultancy services to be requested. It is therefore an opportune time to seek a more streamlined procurement process of consultancy services. The AMG’s Bilateral Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/guidelines-for-programmes-projects-country-strategic-frameworks-and-hard-earmarked-multilat-support) and Financial Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/financial-management) constitute the basic set of procedures for all Danish bilateral development cooperation. The guidelines outline the processes and requirements for the preparation, formulation, quality assurance, approval, implementation, completion and closure of Danish bilateral programmes and projects. The purpose of the framework agreement is to make the MFA procurement of key consultancy services relating to Danish bilateral development programmes and projects more effective and efficient by ensuring quick access to relevant specialists, reducing the procurement time for assignments, and improving the quality of services provided. The objective of the framework agreement is to have a contractual set-up between the MFA and a number of contractors who can provide, upon demand and in a timely manner, the required expertise and service quality for the formulation, appraisal and review of Danish bilateral development programmes and projects. The objective of each assignment and the required outputs will be described in the Terms of Reference, which will be part of the Delivery Contract for the individual assignment. The Framework Agreement solely covers Denmark’s bilateral development cooperation programmes and projects. Therefore, the scope of work of consultancy services solely pertains to Official Development Assistance (ODA) funds. The framework agreement is divided into two lots that reflect the thematic areas and priorities of Denmark’s Strategy for Development Cooperation: Lot 1: Climate, environment, private sector and financing. Lot 2: Governance, fragility, and migration. The framework agreement will require the provision of the following services pertaining to the design and implementation phases of bilateral development cooperation programmes, namely: Formulation of bilateral programmes and projects. This may include preparatory work in the formulation process if and as needed. Appraisal of the design of bilateral programmes and projects as a quality assurance milestone prior to approval. This includes external appraisals led by the consultant and early appraisals of larger or high-risk programmes/projects led by LÆRING. Review of bilateral programmes and projects under implementation. This can span inception, midterm and technical reviews covering the full implementation period of the programme/project as part of the MFA unit’s monitoring and reporting cycle. Reviews do not have the same scope of work, methodology and methods as an evaluation. The MFA’s definition of appraisal, review and evaluation services is aligned with the definitions provided by OECD/DAC (https://one.oecd.org/document/DCD/DAC/EV(2022)2/en/pdf). The content of the services will vary and be defined by the MFA in the specific Terms of Reference for each individual assignment. The following themes and types of services will not be part of the framework agreement: Research and university partnerships. Training programmes and tracer studies. Culture. NGO strategic partnership agreements with the MFA (SPA agreements). Core support to multilateral organisations as described in Danish Organisation Strategies. Strategic Sector Cooperation. Audit assignments. Legal assessments. Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) unit contracts and multi-year MEAL technical assistance. Evaluations. Tender process consultancies. Please refer to the Consultancy Framework Agreement and Appendix 1 Scope of Services for a more detailed description of the object of the procurement.

description: PWGSC, on behalf of Defence Research and Development Canada – Valcartier Research Center, is issuing this Solicitation of offer for the acquisition of Research and Development (R&D) services to develop next-generation C4ISR capabilities to enhance situational awareness and decision-making in multi-domain military operations (land, air, maritime, space, cyber, and information domains). title: Puitejärjestely, murskeiden hankinta 2027-2028
description: Puitejärjestely, murskeiden hankinta 2027-2028 Metsähallitus Metsätalous Oy ja Metsähallitus Luontopalvelut (myöhemmin Metsähallitus) hankkii metsätielle, rakennushankkeisiin sekä purokunnostuksiin murskeita ja kutusoraa joko maa-ainesvarastolta (montulta) tai metsätielle toimitettuna ja levitettynä (sorastuksen palvelukuvaus liite 1). Tarjoaja voi tarjota tarjouksessaan myös myymänsä maa-aineksen kuljetusta, jolloin hän tarjoaa kertoimen suhteessa sorastuksen taksataulukkoon (liite 2). Tarjoaja voi tarjouksessaan kieltäytyä myymästä maa-aineksia muutoin kuin tielle toimitettuna. Tarjouksessa tulee ilmoittaa maa-ainespaikan sijainti ja tarjottavat murskeet hintoineen varastolla. Tarjousten perusteella Metsähallitus hyväksyy toimittajat puitejärjestelyyn. Puitejärjestely alkaa 1.1.2027 ja päättyy 31.12.2028. Tarjottuihin hintoihin sovelletaan liitteen 5 mukaista indeksiehtoa. Sekä tarjottu murskeen hinta että kuljetuksen maksukerroin nousee tai laskee indeksiehdon mukaisesti. Kuhunkin käyttökohteeseen Metsähallitus vertailee puitejärjestelyyn hyväksyttyjen tarjoajien maa-ainespaikkojen sijaintia, tarjontaa ja hintoja. Murske hankitaan kokonaiskustannukseltaan edullisimmalta tarjoajalta. Murskeen monttuhintaan lisätään tällöin kuljetuskustannus murskeen myyjän tai Metsähallituksen sopimuskumppanin kalustolla. Ennen tilausta tai sopimusta tilaaja selvittää saatavuuden tarjoajan yhteyshenkilöltä. Metsähallitus pidättää oikeuden käyttää omia murskeitaan riippumatta puitejärjestelyyn hyväksytyistä tarjouksista. Metsähallitus pidättää myös oikeuden hankkia murskeita muilta toimittajilta, mikäli puitejärjestelyyn hyväksytyiltä maa-ainespaikoilta ei löydy tarvittavaa mursketta kohtuulliselta etäisyydeltä (alle 20 km). Metsähallituksen hallinnoimien alueiden sijainti on esitetty www.retkikartta.fi. Valitse Karttatasot - Metsätalouden monikäyttömetsät - Suojelu- ja retkeilyalueet sekä sopiva taustakartta. Mikäli yksittäisen hankinnan arvo ylittää kansallisen kynnysarvon (60 000 €), siitä laaditaan sopimus (liite 3a). Mikäli yksittäisen hankinnan arvo ylittää EU-kynnysarvon (1.1.2026 alkaen 216 000 €), toimittajan tulee toimittaa rikosrekisteriotteet. Kynnysarvoja pienemmistä hankinnoista Metsähallitus laatii tilauksen (ks. liitteet 3c ja 3d).,

title: Kodinkoneet 2027-2029 Mikalo Oy, Mikkelin asumisoikeus Oy
description: Kodinkoneet 2027-2029 Mikalo Oy, Mikkelin asumisoikeus Oy Mikalo Oy ja Mikkelin Asumisoikeus Oy kilpailuttavat yhdessä kodinkonehankinnat. Hankinnan kohteena on kylmäkoneita, lattialiesiä sekä mikroaaltouuneja. Sopimuskausi on 3 vuotta, ja tilaaja varaa oikeuden hyödyntää kahden (2) vuoden optiokauden. Kaikki laitteet hankitaan kokonaispalveluna asennettuina, ja tarjotun laitehinnan on aina sisällettävä kuljetus, kerroksiinkanto, asennus käyttövalmiiksi, sähkö- tai liitäntätyöt sekä vanhan laitteen poiskuljetus ja kierrätys. Hankinnan laajuus, rajaukset ja sopimuskauden aikaiset muutokset: 1. Mikkelin kaupungin kohteiden rajaus (Ehdollinen optio): Kilpailutuksen tuloksena syntyvää puitejärjestelyä voivat hyödyntää Mikalo Oy:n ja Mikkelin Asumisoikeus Oy:n lisäksi myös Mikkelin kaupunki. Kaupungin osalta sopimus rajataan koskemaan ainoastaan niitä Mikkelin kaupungin omistuksessa olevia vuokra-asuntoja, joita Mikalo Oy isännöi tai ylläpitää. Sopimus ei koske kaupungin muita toimitiloja, virastoja tai laitoksia. Hankintayksikkö pidättää oikeuden laajentaa tilauksia koskemaan näitä kaupungin vuokra-asuntoja, mikäli/jos kyseisiä asuntokantoja siirtyy sopimuskauden aikana suoraan Mikalon hallintaan tai omistukseen. Mikkelin kaupungin osalta tarve koskee satunnaisia ja vähäisiä kodinkonehankintoja sopimuskauden aikana. 2. Uudisrakentaminen, peruskorjaukset ja suurten erien toimitusehdot: Tätä puitesopimusta voidaan hyödyntää vuokrataloyhtiöiden juoksevien arjen korvaushankintojen lisäksi myös hankintayksiköiden omissa uudisrakennus- ja peruskorjauskohteissa (esim. linjasaneeraukset ja perusparannukset). Suurissa peruskorjaus- ja uudiskohteissa, joissa laitteita tilataan kerralla yhteen osoitteeseen yli kymmenen (10) kappaletta, toimitusaika ja logistiikka sovitaan erikseen tapauskohtaisesti hankintayksikön ja toimittajan kesken rakennustyömaan aikataulun mukaan. Mikäli laitteet tilataan peruskorjaus- tai uudiskohteeseen (työmaalle) pelkästään toimitettuna ilman asennusta, tilaaja pyytää toimittajalta tapauskohtaisesti erillisen hyvityksen/alennuksen asennustyön ja vanhan laitteen kierrätyksen osuudesta.,

title: Belgium – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – Purchase, delivery, installation and commissioning of a multi-wavelength orthogonal tomographic volumetric 3D printing system
description: This contract concerns the purchase, delivery, installation, commissioning and handover of a fully operational multi-wavelength orthogonal tomographic volumetric 3D printing system for scientific research. Explanation: The infrastructure is intended for advanced research in tomographic volumetric 3D printing, in which multiple optical wavelengths can be controlled independently to achieve spatial control over different photochemical processes. The system must enable research into multi-wavelength and multi-material tomographic 3D printing. The contract comprises a complete and fully integrated system, including all optical, mechanical and electronic components, light sources, control hardware and software, safety equipment and accessories required for its intended operation. The contract includes delivery of the complete system and all required accessories; installation and commissioning at Ghent University; system configuration, calibration and functional verification; provision of the necessary control and processing software; user training; user and technical documentation; and technical support, warranty and maintenance as further specified in the tender specifications.

title: Netherlands – Sanitary paper products – SARO Europese aanbesteding sanitaire voorzieningen 2026
description: Deze Offerteaanvraag betreft de Europese openbare Aanbesteding Sanitaire voorzieningen waarop de meest recente versie van de Aanbestedingswet 2012 (Aw-2012) van toepassing is. De aanbesteding heeft betrekking op het leveren, beheren, onderhouden en vervangen van sanitaire voorzieningen ten behoeve van Stichting Samen Ambitieus Rotterdams Onderwijs (SARO), hierna tenoemen de Aanbestedende dienst of Opdrachtgever. De geraamde waarde van deze opdracht bedraagt circa € 3 miljoen exclusief btw, inclusief de maximale looptijd van de overeenkomst en alle verlengingsopties. Deze raming is gebaseerd op historische uitgaven van SARO, de huidige omvang van de organisatie, de verwachte gefaseerde instroom van locaties en de uitgangspunten van deze aanbesteding. De raming is indicatief en kan tot ±30% afwijken als gevolg van wijzigingen in locaties, leerling- en medewerkers aantallen, gebruiksintensiteit of andere relevante omstandigheden. Aan deze raming kunnen geen rechten worden ontleend.

title: Weapons Effects Solicitation
description: This solicitation is related to Notice IDs: N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-001 and N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-001_Rev1. The contractor shall provide scientific and technical services with experts in UNDEX and AIREX analysis of undersea and surface vessels to develop and utilize specialized software codes that: 1) Aid in the selection of live fire events and provide support to live fire test and evaluation programs; 2) Simulate an underwater shock environment from a far field or near miss location; 3) Simulate the response of Navy platforms to UNDEX and AIREX for far field, near miss, contact, and internally detonating weapon attacks; 4) Check the integrity of computational models; 5) Solve finite element models elastic-plastic response and reduced order engineering tools to UNDEX and AIREX events; and 6) Simulate a nuclear underwater shock environment or nuclear air blast environment from a far field location. This opportunity is for SEAPORT-NxG MAC HOLDERS ONLY- UNRESTRICTED. No other offers will be considered. Proposals submitted by non-MAC holders will not be evaluated. SeaPort MAC holders will need to register for PIEE accounts in order to receive solicitations and submit proposals/offers. title: Switzerland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Sanierung Bodensee-Arena Leistungsofferte HLKS inkl. Gebäudeautomation und Fachkoordination
description: La Bodensee-Arena est un complexe sportif, de loisirs et d'événements majeur de la région de Kreuzlingen-Constance. Créé en 1978 et agrandi à plusieurs reprises, ce complexe présente un besoin important de rénovation sur les plans architectural, technique et opérationnel. La ville de Kreuzlingen prévoit la rénovation du complexe existant et la transformation de l'actuelle patinoire extérieure en salle d'entraînement. La structure existante doit être réutilisée dans la mesure où cela s’avère techniquement et économiquement justifié. La réalisation se fera par étapes, en tenant compte de l’exploitation en cours. Le crédit d’investissement de 26,7 millions de francs suisses a été approuvé lors du référendum du 28 septembre 2025. Ce montant constitue le plafond financier contraignant de l’ensemble du projet. La conception doit être développée de manière cohérente selon le principe du « Design-to-Cost ». Dans le cadre d’une procédure d’appel d’offres sélective avec préqualification (phase 1) suivie d’une soumission d’offres (phase 2), un bureau d’études qualifié en CVC est recherché pour la conception CVC, y compris l’automatisation du bâtiment (MSRL) et la coordination technique. Le bureau doit couvrir l’ensemble des domaines techniques faisant l’objet de l’appel d’offres et assumer la responsabilité globale de la coordination et de l’intégration des prestations dans le cadre du mandat. Le mandat comprend les prestations prévues par la norme SIA 108 pour les phases 31 à 53, de la conception à la mise en service. Les différents niveaux de modernisation des installations techniques existantes, l'intégration de la récupération de la chaleur résiduelle provenant du système de refroidissement de la patinoire, ainsi que la coordination de l'approvisionnement en énergie et des installations techniques dans le bâtiment principal existant et dans la nouvelle salle d'entraînement constituent des défis particuliers. Il s’agit de trouver des solutions économiques et efficaces sur le plan énergétique, qui tiennent compte des différentes utilisations et conditions d’exploitation et permettent une réalisation par étapes tout en préservant autant que possible le fonctionnement courant. Les interfaces avec les études de réfrigération et d’électricité, faisant l’objet de marchés distincts, doivent être assurées.

title: Switzerland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Sanierung Bodensee-Arena Leistungsofferte Elektroplanung
description: La Bodensee-Arena est un complexe sportif, de loisirs et d'événements majeur de la région de Kreuzlingen-Constance. Créé en 1978 et agrandi à plusieurs reprises, ce complexe présente un besoin important de rénovation sur les plans architectural, technique et opérationnel. La ville de Kreuzlingen prévoit la rénovation du complexe existant et la transformation de l'actuelle patinoire extérieure en salle d'entraînement. La structure existante doit être réutilisée dans la mesure où cela s’avère techniquement et économiquement justifié. La réalisation se fera par étapes, en tenant compte de l’exploitation en cours. Le crédit d’investissement de 26,7 millions de francs suisses a été approuvé lors du référendum du 28 septembre 2025. Il constitue le plafond financier contraignant de l’ensemble du projet. La conception doit être développée de manière cohérente selon le principe du « Design-to-Cost ». Dans le cadre d’une procédure d’appel d’offres sélective avec préqualification (phase 1) suivie d’une soumission d’offres (phase 2), un bureau d’études en électrotechnique qualifié est recherché pour la conception électrique, y compris les installations photovoltaïques. Le mandat comprend les prestations prévues par la norme SIA 108 pour les phases 31 à 53, de la conception à la mise en service, y compris la conception des installations à courant fort et à courant faible ainsi que des installations photovoltaïques. Les différents niveaux de modernisation des installations électriques existantes, le renouvellement des câbles et des tableaux de distribution, ainsi que l’intégration des installations photovoltaïques dans l’infrastructure électrique constituent des défis particuliers. La conception doit tenir compte des différentes utilisations et conditions d’exploitation de l’actuelle Bodensee-Arena et de la nouvelle salle d’entraînement, et permettre une réalisation par étapes tout en préservant autant que possible le fonctionnement courant. Les interfaces avec les systèmes CVC et d’automatisation du bâtiment, pour lesquels des marchés distincts ont été passés, avec la conception du système de refroidissement de la patinoire ainsi qu’avec la protection contre l’incendie doivent être coordonnées et validées dès le début du projet. Nous recherchons des solutions économiques, efficaces sur le plan énergétique et fiables, qui répondent aux exigences de l’ensemble du projet et respectent le plafond budgétaire imposé.

title: Oakengates Carnival and Parade - Organisation and Delivery
description: Oakengates Town Council is looking to appoint a qualified and experienced event management company to organise and deliver a carnival and parade in Oakengates, Telford in the Summer of 2027 (date to be agreed). Under the direction of the Council, the successful bidder will be responsible, for the following: • Event Planning and Coordination: develop a comprehensive plan for the carnival, including timelines, logistics, and contingency plans. • Entertainment and Activities: arrange for a diverse range of entertainment options, including live performances, games, and interactive activities. • Vendor Management: coordinate with food and merchandise vendors to ensure a wide variety of offerings. • Marketing and Promotion: develop and execute a marketing strategy to promote the event and attract attendees. • Health and Safety: ensure all health and safety regulations are met, including crowd control, first aid, and emergency procedures. • Income Generation - identify potential income generating opportunities to support the cost of the event. • Post-Event Evaluation: provide a detailed report on the event's success, including attendance figures, feedback and recommendations for future events. Interested companies are required to submit the following: • Company Profile: a brief overview of the company, including relevant experience and qualifications. • Proposed Plan: a detailed proposal outlining the approach to organising and delivering the carnival and parade. • Budget: a comprehensive budget breakdown, including all anticipated costs. • Insurance: evidence of public liability • References: contact information for at least two previous clients who can attest to the company's capabilities. Late submissions will not be considered and Oakengates Town Council reserves the right to accept or reject any or all bids. All costs incurred in the preparation of the bid are the responsibility of the bidding company. Prospective contractors must not contact Councillors or staff to encourage or support their tender outside the prescribed process. Written tenders must be received by Oakengates Town Council in a sealed envelope marked 'Oakengates Town Council - Carnival Tender' and addressed to the Town Clerk, by 5pm on Tuesday 24 November 2026 and should be sent to: Oakengates Town Council The Wakes, Theatre Square Telford, TF2 6EP If you require any further information, please contact Oakengates Town Council by: Email: townclerk@oakengates-tc.gov.uk, or telephone: 01952 567500

title: Request for Information (RFI) for a Cislunar Space System (CSS)
description: (U) The Department of the Air Force (DAF) is seeking market research information to inform the potential acquisition strategy for a Cislunar Space System (CSS). The CSS will consist of up to five (5) space vehicles (SVs), each of which will require a spacecraft bus, accommodation of a Government-provided payload, SV integration & test, a Ground Segment, including mission management and telemetry, tracking, control and communications, a solution for space launch, system (space vehicle/ground segment/communications) integration, and operations and maintenance (O&M). The Government is notionally interested in procuring up to five (5) SVs to meet DAF mission needs in late CY29. These vehicles may serve as seed vehicles that will inform the acquisition strategy for a potential future proliferated cislunar constellation. The Government is looking for information on industry's ability to provide a rapid, low-risk (minimal non-recurring engineering (NRE)) solution that can accommodate the Government's technical and programmatic objectives. (U) The Government intends to award up to five (5) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) preliminary design study contracts upon Government consideration of the market information collected with this RFI and all other sources of information relevant to the effort. Failure to respond to this RFI may result in loss of the ability to participate in a subsequent program acquisition. (U) This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), and industry should not construe the RFI as a commitment by the Government. title: Request for Information (RFI) for a Cislunar Space System (CSS)
description: (U) The Department of the Air Force (DAF) is seeking market research information to inform the potential acquisition strategy for a Cislunar Space System (CSS). The CSS will consist of up to five (5) space vehicles (SVs), each of which will require a spacecraft bus, accommodation of a Government-provided payload, SV integration & test, a Ground Segment, including mission management and telemetry, tracking, control and communications, a solution for space launch, system (space vehicle/ground segment/communications) integration, and operations and maintenance (O&M). The Government is notionally interested in procuring up to five (5) SVs to meet DAF mission needs in late CY29. These vehicles may serve as seed vehicles that will inform the acquisition strategy for a potential future proliferated cislunar constellation. The Government is looking for information on industry's ability to provide a rapid, low-risk (minimal non-recurring engineering (NRE)) solution that can accommodate the Government's technical and programmatic objectives. (U) The Government intends to award up to five (5) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) preliminary design study contracts upon Government consideration of the market information collected with this RFI and all other sources of information relevant to the effort. Failure to respond to this RFI may result in loss of the ability to participate in a subsequent program acquisition. (U) This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), and industry should not construe the RFI as a commitment by the Government. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) provision 15.101, Early Exchanges with Industry, be advised that this is only an RFI and does not obligate the Government to reimburse any cost associated with preparation and/or submission of a RFI response. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes only solicitation. Offers are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation Number FA281627R0003 is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ). The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract to provide waste management services for Los Angeles Air Force Base. The Contractor shall furnish all personnel, equipment, labor, tools, materials, supervision, transportation, permits, disposal fees, containers, collection vehicles, and other items and services necessary to perform waste management services at Los Angeles Air Force Base, El Segundo, California, and any other locations identified in the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS) or Statement of Work (SOW). Services may include, as specified in the PWS/SOW: Collection, transportation, and disposal of municipal solid waste; Collection, transportation, and recycling of recyclable materials; Provision, maintenance, repair, and replacement of waste and recycling containers; Scheduled and unscheduled collection services; Disposal documentation, manifests, weight tickets, and recycling reports; Compliance with applicable federal, state, local, and installation environmental, safety, and waste-disposal requirements; and Other waste-management support requirements identified in the PWS/SOW. This acquisition is 100 percent full and open. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 562111, with a corresponding small-business size standard of $47,000,000.00. The applicable Product Service Code (PSC) is S205. Line Items, Quantities, Units of Measure, and Options All contract line-item number (CLIN) information, quantities, units of measure, periods of performance, and option periods are contained in the attached SF 1449 and pricing schedule. Offerors shall provide pricing for all base and option CLINs. Quotations that omit pricing for any required CLIN or option period may be determined ineligible for award. Place of Performance Los Angeles Air Force Base 483 N. Aviation Blvd. El Segundo, CA 90245-2808 Additional performance locations, if applicable, will be identified in the attached PWS/SOW. Provisions and Clauses The following provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition: FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors�Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR 52.212-3, Offeror Representations and Certifications�Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR 52.212-5, Contract Terms and Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders�Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services FAR 52.217-9, Option to Extend the Term of the Contract Instructions to offerors and evaluation factors under FAR 52.212-1 and FAR 52.212-2 are contained in the attached SF 1449. Offerors must follow the attached instructions when preparing and submitting a quotation. Quotation Submission Requirements Quotations shall not exceed 10 pages, excluding the completed SF 1449 pricing schedule and any required representations and certifications. Pages exceeding the 10-page limit will not be evaluated. Each quotation shall include: Company profile; Primary point of contact information; Small-business type/status; Applicable NAICS code; Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code; Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); Completed SF 1449 pricing spreadsheet using the Government-provided template and matching the required CLIN structure; A technical approach describing the offeror�s ability to perform the waste management services described in the PWS/SOW; Identification of proposed collection schedules, equipment, container types, disposal/recycling methods, and quality-control procedures, as applicable; and Completed FAR 52.212-3 representations and certifications. Incomplete quotations may be determined ineligible for award. Due Dates: 24 November 2026 Questions: All questions concerning this requirement must be submitted by email no later than November 6, 2026 @ 12 pm PST. Submit questions to roderick.jones.1@spaceforce.mil, with dalice.va@spaceforce.mil copied. Quotes: Quotations must be submitted by email no later than November 20th@ 12pm PST. Submit quotations to roderick.jones.1@spaceforce.mil, dalice.va @spaceforce.mil.

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Marshalling Services Idaho Falls, ID
description: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � April 30, 2030 in Idaho Falls, ID. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Idaho Falls, ID area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. To facilitate this process, GSA Fleet employs its vehicle remarketing specialists, who are warranted sales contracting officers and experts in the sales of its vehicles, to work with its vendors to approve repairs, pricing, as well as carry out and approve each sale to maximize net proceeds. description: This is an offer for a to provide MRRIC Chair professional services, in close coordination with MRRIC, the lead agency, and one or more meeting facilitators. Services include supporting the diverse Committee members as an impartial leader in enabling members to articulate their underlying interests and perspectives and help the Committee formulate consensus-based recommendations to the lead agency as it relates to the USACE MRRP and assist the USACE in planning and leading constructive MRRIC engagements per the Performance Work Statement (PWS)

title: RFI Contractor F-16 Pilot Services
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Title: �RFI Contractor F-16 Pilot Services� Notice ID: FA823226ACFERRY USAF/AFMC/AFLCMC/F-16-SPO/FMS Contracting Office, Hill Air Force Base, UT Description 1.1 The F-16 Support Program Office in support of the FMS countries is seeking information on how an interested contractor could provide Contractor F-16 Pilot Services � Ferry Flight Operations for Two (2) F-16 Block 52 Fighting Falcon Aircraft (Lockheed Martin Facility, Greenville, SC to Martyr BG Ali Flaih AB, Iraq) 1.2 THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force is not at this time seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it could possibly be synopsized on the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement; however, if you do provide information, you could possibly be sent the solicitation notification directly and this is NOT guaranteed. Background 2.1 The United States Government (USG) has an emerging requirement to execute a point-to-point ferry flight delivery of two (2) F-16 Fighting Falcon (Block 52) aircraft originating from the Lockheed Martin Facility in Greenville, South Carolina (Lockheed Martin F-16 Production and Sustainment Facility, Donaldson Field / KGYH) to Martyr BG Ali Flaih Air Base in the Republic of Iraq. 2.2 Anticipated Execution Period: March 2027. 2.3 Pre-Mission Integration & Approvals: Q1 FY2027 / January�February 2027 (flight records review, GFR approvals, ALSS inspections, APACS clearances, Lockheed Martin site access/badging, and AMC Coronet coordination). 2.4 Operational Division of Responsibility: Contractor Responsibility: Furnish two (2) fully qualified, current, and mission-capable F-16 Block 50/52 Pilot-in-Command (PIC) aviators (plus one designated alternate) to conduct the flight operations. Ensure flight crew compliance with theater entry, medical readiness, survival training standards, and badging/facility access protocols at the Lockheed Martin Greenville facility. Program Office Responsibility: All aircraft maintenance support, pre-/post-flight inspections, en-route servicing, and technical troubleshooting will be coordinated directly by the USG Program Office (e.g., AFLCMC Program Office / designated depot field service teams) in coordination with Lockheed Martin facility personnel prior to release. AMC / ACC Responsibility: All aerial refueling (AAR) support, tanker boom operations, Coronet flight movements, and military oceanic flight plans will be scheduled and coordinated through Air Mobility Command (AMC) and Air Combat Command (ACC). 2.5 Objective The primary objectives of this market research notice are to: Identify commercial sources capable of providing two (2) qualified F-16 Block 52 ferry pilots with documented currency, Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-229 operational familiarity, boom aerial refueling certifications, and international long-range flight experience ready for deployment from the Lockheed Martin Greenville facility to Martyr BG Ali Flaih AB in March 2027. Assess industry capacity to integrate into US Air Force operational flight packages (e.g., cell formation flying and Coronet missions supported by AMC tanker assets) and coordinate closely with Program Office maintenance and plant representatives. Evaluate compliance mechanisms under Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Instruction 8210.1 and Government Flight Representative (GFR) flight crew approval processes operating from a contractor/OEM facility. Solicit industry feedback regarding life support equipment provisioning, survival certifications, theater entry lead times, weather delay/standby structures, and mobilization horizons leading into March 2027. 2.6 Scope of Work and Technical Requirements Areas Task Area 1: Pilot Qualifications, Credentials, and Currency The contractor shall supply two (2) primary ferry pilots and one (1) designated backup/alternate pilot meeting the following mandatory thresholds: Flight Hours & Airframe Currency: Minimum 1,500 total military/tactical flight hours, with at least 500 hours as Pilot-in-Command (PIC) in the F-16. Documented PIC qualification and currency in the F-16 Block 50/52 configuration (Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-229 engine familiarity). Documented F-16 flight currency leading up to the March 2027 departure date (including instrument, formation, and emergency procedures). Aerial Refueling (AAR) Qualification: Current or recent qualification in military boom aerial refueling (day and night tanker receiver procedures) compatible with USAF KC-135, KC-10, or KC-46 tankers. Survival Training & Physiological Standards: Valid Water Survival / Underwater Egress Training (Dunker/HUET) certification current within standard service intervals for oceanic crossings. Valid Physiological / High-Altitude Chamber training (or altitude chamber refresher) compliant with USAF standards. Basic Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape (SERE) familiarization or tactical isolated personnel guidance appropriate for operations into the CENTCOM AOR. Licensing & Medical Certifications: Valid FAA Commercial or Airline Transport Pilot (ATP) Certificate with instrument rating, or military equivalent documentation (DD Form 759 / Flight Record). Current FAA Class I Medical Certificate (or military flight physical equivalent) valid through the planned mission window in March 2027, along with CENTCOM medical deployment readiness/waiver screening. Security Clearance, COMSEC & Facility Access: Active U.S. Secret security clearance (or higher) to handle classified flight route data, secure tactical communication suites (e.g., Have Quick, ARC-210), and Mode 4/5 IFF systems. Eligibility for security vetting and unescorted flight line badge access at the Lockheed Martin Greenville facility. Task Area 2: Operational Coordination and Mission Execution Pre-Flight at Lockheed Martin Facility and Operations with AMC/ACC: Report to the Lockheed Martin facility in Greenville, SC for mission planning, final pre-flight walkarounds, cockpit checks, and coordination with Program Office and DCMA plant personnel. Integrate into AMC Coronet movement planning, mission briefings, and cell lead/trail formation procedures scheduled for the March 2027 movement. Coordinate with Program Office maintenance personnel for aircraft acceptance, debriefings, and aircraft turnover at intermediate staging points and final delivery. Conduct pre-flight route briefings, weather checks, oceanic contingency planning, and divert emergency reviews alongside government tanker/escort crews. DCMA 8210.1 & GFR Approval: Compliance with DCMA Instruction 8210.1 (Contractor's Flight and Ground Operations). Submission of flight crew records, training certificates, and medical approvals to the cognizant Government Flight Representative (GFR) for flight crew qualification approval at least 45 days prior to the March 2027 departure. Theater Entry, International Clearances, and Repatriation: Ensure all flight crew members maintain valid U.S. Passports (minimum 6 months validity past mission window), required en-route transit visas, and Iraqi entry documentation. Coordinate country clearance submissions via the Aircraft Clearance Processing System (APACS) and contractor tracking through the Synchronized Predeployment and Opera

Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales process. To facilitate this process, GSA Fleet employs its vehicle remarketing specialists, who are warranted sales contracting officers and experts in the sales of its vehicles, to work with its vendors to approve repairs, pricing, as well as carry out and approve each sale to maximize net proceeds. REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROVISIONS - NOT APPLICABLE. 5. PACKAGING- MIL-STD 2073 PACKAGING APPLIES AS FOUND ELSEWHERE IN THE SCHEDULE 6. NOTES - NOT APPLICABLE

title: CBRND Seeking Aircraft Interior Decontamination Technology
description: The Department of War (DoW), Portfolio Management Executive for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (PME CBRND), Joint Project Manager for CBRN Special Operations Forces (JPM CBRN SOF) is seeking information, design concepts, and mature technology capabilities for a Tactical Aircraft Interior Decontamination Dispersal System. The goal of this initiative is to identify or evaluate a mature, rapidly deployable, and highly reliable hardware applicator system capable of delivering fine-aerosol, dry-fog, or gaseous decontaminants uniformly throughout military aircraft interiors without damaging sensitive electronics. Key Technical Parameters & Scope: Dispersal Mechanics: Must disperse a fine aerosol/dry fog with a Volume Median Diameter (VMD) of less than 10 microns (Threshold) or a gas-phase molecular dispersion less than 0.001 microns (Objective) to maximize surface coverage without wetting, pooling, or dripping. Tactical Mobility & Footprint: Must fit securely within a Polaris MRZR cargo bed with a stowed envelope not exceeding 42" H x 18" D x 18" W (Threshold), with a target envelope under 30" H x 14" D x 16" W (Objective) to allow upright walk-through clearance in CH-47 and CV-22 cabins. System Weight: Empty chassis weight must be ? 150 lbs (Threshold) for a 4-man lift, with a target empty weight of ? 100 lbs (Objective) for a 2-man lift. Fully loaded weight with maximum consumables must not exceed 500 lbs. Power Flexibility: Operable from standard single-phase 110-120 VAC (50/60 Hz), commercial/tactical generators ? 6 kW, or vehicle auxiliary 28 VDC (Threshold), with a target capability to interface directly with utility and flight-line power IAW MIL-STD-704 (Objective). Employment Versatility: Must support two primary delivery modes: Internal cabin placement on medium/heavy aircraft (CH-47, CV-22, C-130) and external ducting/pumping into constrained cockpits (AH/MH-6 Little Bird). Material Compatibility: All wetted paths, seals, pumps, and nozzles must demonstrate broad chemical compatibility with existing and emerging USG-standard decontaminants, including aqueous hydrogen peroxide ($H_2O_2$), modified amine/ammonia solutions, Dahlgren Decon, and JGPD. System Modularity: Complete operational system must consist of 5 or fewer major items (Threshold), with a target of a single, all-in-one consolidated chassis (Objective) containing integrated internal stowage for all cords, hoses, and nozzles. Technology Maturity: The core dispersal technology must be at a demonstrated Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 or higher in a relevant operating environment to support near-term military evaluation and procurement.

title: Kansallinen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelu
description: Kansallinen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelu Maa- ja metsätalousministeriö (”hankintayksikkö”) vastaa ilmastonmuutokseen sopeutumistyön koordinoinnista valtioneuvostotasolla. Ministeriö vastaa kansallisen ilmastonmuutokseen sopeutumissuunnitelman ja sen taustamateriaalien (ml. kansallisen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun) valmistelusta ilmastolain mukaisesti. Maa- ja metsätalousministeriön tarkoituksena on hankkia valtakunnallisen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun suunnittelu, toteutus ja raportointi. Riski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun tulosten tulisi olla käytettävissä, kun kansallisen sopeutumissuunnitelman valmistelu aloitetaan seuraavan vaalikauden alussa. Kansallisen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun valmistelun tavoitteena on saada parhaaseen käytettävissä olevaan tietoon perustuva käsitys Suomeen kohdistuvista ilmasto-riskeistä ja haavoittuvuuksista sekä vahvistaa yhteyttä riskien ja haavoittuvuuksien arvioinnin ja sopeutumispolitiikan suunnittelun välillä. Tarkastelun tulee tukea nykyistä vahvemmin sopeutumistoimien kohdentamista niihin riskeihin, vaikutuksiin ja haavoittuvuuksiin, joiden arvioidaan olevan merkittävimpiä suomalaiselle yhteiskunnalle. Samalla tarkastelun tulisi tunnistaa uusia tai tarkentaa tietoa aiemmin tunnistetuista riskeistä sekä kuvata mahdollisia tietopuutteita. Ilmastolaki edellyttää alueellista tarkastelua tarpeen mukaan. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu liitteessä 1 Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus.,
